lines.say: Mortgage rates just fell four weeks in a row. Here's the catch.

lines.text: Freddie Mac's survey, out today: the average 30-year fixed rate is 7.11%.
lines.say: Freddie Mac's survey, out today, puts the average thirty-year fixed rate at about seven point one percent.

lines.text: That's down from 7.40% in early October, the highest in nearly three years.
lines.say: That's down from about seven point four in early October, the highest in nearly three years.

lines.text: On a $400,000 loan, that's about $79 a month less (our math).
lines.say: On a four hundred thousand dollar loan, that's about seventy-nine dollars a month less, by our math.

lines.text: The catch? A year ago, it was 6.24%.
lines.say: The catch? A year ago, it was about six point two percent.

lines.text: That same loan cost about $231 a month less back then (our math).
lines.say: That same loan cost about two hundred thirty-one dollars a month less back then.

lines.text: What moves them? Mortgage rates tend to follow the 10-year Treasury yield, not the Fed directly.
lines.say: What moves them? Mortgage rates tend to follow the ten-year Treasury yield, not the Fed directly.

lines.text: That average assumes 20% down and strong credit, so your quote can differ.
lines.say: And that average assumes twenty percent down and strong credit, so your quote can differ.
Next Thursday's update shows whether the streak makes it to five.

post.title: Mortgage rates fell 4 weeks straight. Here's the catch.
post.ig:
Mortgage rates just fell four weeks in a row. Here's the catch.
The average 30-year fixed rate is 7.11%, down from 7.18% last week (Freddie Mac, Nov 12, 2026).
It peaked at 7.40% in early October, the highest in nearly three years.
But a year ago it was 6.24%. On a $400,000 loan, that's about $231 a month more today (our math).
Sources: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey; AP.
News and education, not financial advice.
